title: Enterprise compliance intake scoring engine and action orchestra
creator: Ayesha Patel
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers repeatedly submit security and compliance requests (SOC2 evidence requests, ISO questionnaires, HIPAA attestations, GDPR/DPA demands, vendor questionnaires). Current intake is ad-hoc: requests land in email, Support, or a shared drive and require manual routing to Legal/Security/Engineering. This creates long SLAs, duplicated work, and inconsistent prioritization.

Goal: Build a repeatable, explainable scoring engine and orchestration pipeline that automatically classifies and prioritizes inbound security/compliance asks, attaches the correct SLA and review path, and surfaces required product changes or documentation gaps. The system should reduce manual triage time, give predictable response times to sales/CS, and allow product teams to plan capacity for Private/Dedicated/Hosted compliance work.

Scope: intake channels (Support ticket, Sales handoff, self-serve form), initial automatic scoring, assignment rules (Legal, InfoSec, Product), SLA bands, and an audit log. Excludes in-depth legal contract negotiation and custom contract drafting (handled by Legal).
acceptance_criteria: AC1: New intake form and Support integration reliably tags requests with a request-type and raw metadata (data types, customer size, jurisdiction)
AC2: Scoring engine computes a reproducible score based on defined factors and returns one of three priority bands: Low / Medium / High
AC3: High-priority requests automatically create a dedicated ticket in Legal with prefilled evidence checklist and 24h SLA flag
AC4: Medium-priority requests route to Security/Product queue with 5 business day SLA and suggested mitigations/answers
AC5: Low-priority requests are queued to Docs/FAQ backlog and get templated responses; all automated responses include justification of score
AC6: Dashboard displays throughput, average time-to-ack, and evidence completion rate by request type
AC7: Full audit trail and exportable CSV of scored attributes for post-mortem and model tuning
tasks: T1: Design intake form (Support + Sales) and capture schema (sensitivity, PHI? PII? export scope?, jurisdiction, contract value)
T2: Define scoring rubric and weightings for factors: data sensitivity, contract tier, regulatory scope, timeline urgency, product impact, regional law applicability
T3: Build Light-weight scoring microservice and Linear webhook integration
T4: Implement routing rules to Legal/Security/Product and automated SLA flags
T5: Create templated evidence bundles for common asks (SOC2 sysdescr, encryption docs, DPA template, HIPAA controls mapping)
T6: Console dashboard and metrics (MVP: throughput, median ack time, % completed on SLA)
T7: Run a two-week pilot with Sales and two enterprise customers and collect feedback
T8: Iterate on thresholds and false-positive reduction; finalize runbook for responders
comments: 2025-02-12 - Ayesha Patel: Kickoff complete. Aligned with Legal and InfoSec on high-level scoring factors. Legal emphasized that contract-level asks must bubble to a human review despite a high score.

2025-02-20 - Liam Chen: Implemented initial scoring prototype. Uses five weighted factors (sensitivity, contractual threshold, regulatory jurisdiction, timeline urgency, product-change-needed). Prototype available in GitHub PR linked above.

2025-02-25 - Priya Reddy (Security): Reviewed prototype. Feedback: increase weight for 'PHI present' and add 'is customer in EU' binary factor for GDPR workload. Also flagged storage of questionnaire attachments - must be encrypted-at-rest with KMS-protected keys.
2025-03-01 - Ayesha Patel: Pilot scheduled with Sales AE team and two customers (ACME Corp and BioMed Inc) for 2025-03-10 to validate score thresholds and response templates.
2025-03-04 - Legal (Jon Ortiz): Approved routing and evidence checklist for High-priority SOC2/ISO requests. Requested a manual override flag on tickets for contract negotiations.
